competences: The learner identifies key facts about the constitution.
The learner explains information about Meaning, functions and importance of a constitution using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes constitution, supreme law, rights.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about the constitution.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Meaning, functions and importance of a constitution.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about the constitution.
materials: Primary Five SST reference on Meaning, functions and importance of a constitution
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces the constitution. They ask "What is a national constitution" and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about the constitution
steps.content: A constitution is the supreme law of the country. A constitution is a set of laws by which a country is governed. Or Uganda has had four constitutions since her independence. Namely; The 1962 constitution which led Uganda to independence . It made provisions for the position of the president and the prime minister. The 1966 constitution / pigeon hole constitution . In 1966, there were conflicts between The 1967 constitution which was known as the Republican constitution. The past constitutions were not suitable for modern Uganda. The citizens were not consulted during the making of the old constitution. How the views were collected from the citizens The constitutional commission was formed to collect views from the citizens.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the constitution on the chalkboard, including "A constitution is the supreme law of the country.; A constitution is a set of laws by which a country is governed. Or". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about the constitution
steps.content: He was the head of the constitutional commission which collected views from the citizens/ drafted it. A Constitution is a set of laws governing an real organization A national constitution is a set of laws by which a country is governed Constitution sets the duration for conducting general elections Constitution sets conditions to participate in general elections Unwritten constitution Results of the Republican constitution It replaced the 1995 constitution Qn: Why was the 1995 constitution referref to as the people’s It was the day when the 1995 constitution was made known to the public /Launched Justice Benjamin Odoki Qn: How was the constitution review commission important
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the constitution on the chalkboard, including "He was the head of the constitutional commission which collected views from the citizens/ drafted it.; A Constitution is a set of laws governing an real organization". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about the constitution
steps.content: It collected people’s views about the constitution Qn: Write C.A.D in full It was not popular because it was not discussed by the parliament. (iii) The 1967 constitution. It was also called the Republican constitution. Results of the 1967 constitution. The president was given more powers to rule the country than the prime minister. (iv) The 1995 constitution. The constituent Assembly Delegates (a group of people with the power to change the constitution) were elected in 1994. Justice Benjamin Odoki was the head of the constitutional commission that collected views from the majority of the citizens all over the country. Note: This was the constitution which led Uganda to independence. It was replaced by the 1966 constitution. It replaced the 1962 constitution
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about the constitution on the chalkboard, including "It collected people’s views about the constitution Qn: Write C.A.D in full; It was not popular because it was not discussed by the parliament. (iii) The 1967 constitution.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: What is a national constitution | Write down any two constitutions that Uganda has had since independence. | Why is a constitution important in a democratic country like Uganda? | Mention the way, the 1967 constitution was unfriendly to the kingdoms in Uganda. | Who head the constitutional review commission?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "What is a national constitution" and "Write down any two constitutions that Uganda has had since independence.". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on the constitution, asks "What is a national constitution" and follows up with "Write down any two constitutions that Uganda has had since independence.". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "What is a national constitution" and "Write down any two constitutions that Uganda has had since independence.", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "Why was the 1966 constitution also called pigeon hole constitution?"
